title: Supreme Court Clears 'Mahaprabhu Jagannath' Animated Film for Release After Rath Yatra
excerpt: Supreme Court allows release of 'Mahaprabhu Jagannath' animated film after Rath Yatra on July 28.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Supreme Court allows release of 'Mahaprabhu Jagannath' animated film after Rath Yatra on July 28.
  • Orissa High Court had blocked the film's release, citing potential harm to religious sentiments.
  • Film received CBFC certification and will be shown in over 300 theaters across multiple languages.
  • International release planned for the US, Canada, and Europe following the Indian debut.

Key Takeaways

  • India's Supreme Court has permitted the nationwide release of animated film Mahaprabhu Jagannath on or after July 28, overturning an Orissa High Court stay order.
  • The High Court had blocked the film's scheduled July 17 release, ruling it could hurt religious sentiments during the ongoing Rath Yatra festival in Puri.
  • Justices BV Nagarathna and R Mahadevan noted the film had received CBFC certification and questioned how an animated film could diminish devotion.
  • The film, produced by Bhubaneswar-based Ele Animations, was set for release across 300+ theatres in Hindi, Odia, and Telugu, with an international rollout planned for the US, Canada, and Europe.

Supreme Court Overturns High Court Stay

India's Supreme Court on Friday permitted the nationwide release of the animated film Mahaprabhu Jagannath on or after July 28, setting aside an Orissa High Court interim order that had blocked the film's theatrical debut just hours before its scheduled July 17 premiere.

A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and R Mahadevan noted that the annual Rath Yatra festival in Puri would continue until July 27 and allowed the exhibition to begin once the festivities conclude. "We permit the film to be exhibited on or after 28th July," the court stated in its order in Ele Animations Pvt Ltd v. Mahesh Kumar Sahu.

https://youtu.be/1s3Yxnd5BM0

How the Legal Battle Unfolded

> **""We want to know how, by an animation film, how the devotion of the writ petitioners comes down?"**

The controversy began after the film's teaser drew objections from the Shree Jagannath Temple Administration and others over certain depictions of Lord Jagannath. The producers screened the film before the Temple Administration and the Gajapati Maharaja of Puri, who requested changes to specific scenes. The filmmakers went ahead with the July 17 release date without incorporating those changes, according to court filings.

A public interest litigation petition was filed before the Orissa High Court seeking revocation of the film's CBFC certificate and a restraining order on its release. The High Court granted interim relief, observing that freedom of speech had to be balanced against restrictions under Article 19(2) of the Constitution and that releasing the film during Rath Yatra could be "counterproductive." The stay order was uploaded at 9 p.m. the night before the scheduled release, leaving producers with virtually no time to respond.

Senior Advocate Devadatt Kamat, appearing for the filmmakers before the Supreme Court, argued the delay would cause substantial financial losses. Bookings had been made across nearly 300 theatres nationwide, and crores of rupees had been invested in the production. Kamat submitted that the Central Board of Film Certification had already granted a U certificate under the Cinematograph Act, clearing the film for Hindi, Odia, and Telugu audiences.

![Orissa High Court — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b9/Odisha_High_Court.JPG)

The Court's Reasoning

Justice Nagarathna directly questioned the basis of the objections. "We want to know how, by an animation film, how the devotion of the writ petitioners comes down? It will not come down," she remarked during the hearing, according to Bar and Bench.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the State of Odisha, told the court that traditional authorities had found certain depictions objectionable, including portrayals of Lord Jagannath in combat scenes. "The traditional heads found certain parts to be objectionable. The way the lord is shown fighting... There are certain issues," Mehta submitted.

The court recorded that a television series based on the same subject — Ele Animations' Jay Jagannath — had already been exhibited on YouTube without similar objections, a point that appeared to weigh in the filmmakers' favor.

What the Film Is About

Produced by Bhubaneswar-based Ele Animations Pvt Ltd and directed by Shripad Warkhedkar, Mahaprabhu Jagannath is a family-oriented animated feature set in the mythological universe of Lord Jagannath. The storyline follows Mahaprabhu Jagannath, along with Balram and Garud, on a journey across realms to rescue devotees trapped by a powerful demon named Aham. The film is distributed in partnership with Cinépolis and features voice performances by Prachi Save Saathi, Sonal Kaushal, and Aadityaraj Sharma.

Producer Durga Prasad Dalai issued a statement describing the film as "an extension of our animated series Jay Jagannath, created with the utmost honesty, sincerity and devotion for Lord Jagannath and His devotees."

Diaspora Angle

The film had planned an international release in the US, Canada, and Europe alongside its Indian debut. The 11-day delay pushes those overseas screenings to late July at the earliest, though the Supreme Court order clears the path for the international rollout to proceed after July 28. Baba Ramdev had publicly endorsed the film as a way to teach children Sanatan values.

What's Next

The matter is posted for further hearing on August 5. The Rath Yatra concludes on July 27, and the film can begin its theatrical run the following day. Whether the filmmakers will need to incorporate changes requested by the Puri Temple Administration before the next hearing remains an open question. The CBFC certification, however, stands — the Supreme Court did not disturb it.
